extraction_hazards: SOURCE DEFECT: the first criteria list has no lead-in sentence, so it is a list of bare diagnoses with no 'meets the definition of medical necessity for ...' verb; a parser cannot know the list is coverage (not exclusion) without the title/context.
The Position Statement begins with a 'Note:' that sets scope before the list, so the first line after the heading is not criteria.
Description's 'Summary and Analysis of Evidence' includes author-year citations in parentheses.
OTHER lists brand names (CyberKnife, NeuroMate) that are illustrative only.

Update history mentions a 'decision tree' (05/15/14) and ICD-10 updates that no longer appear in the document; the history is the only place a reader learns the Karnofsky Performance Scale was deleted (03/15/21), leaving 'good performance status' undefined.
interesting_structures: Pure indication lists: coverage by diagnosis membership, almost no clinical conditions.
Two lists (first-course and re-irradiation) with overlapping entries.
Defect-as-hazard: the 'any of these indications' semantics is implicit.

fit_to_tree.why: An 'any' over about 12 diagnosis leaves, a few with one extra condition; easy to model once the missing lead-in is handled by convention, but qualifiers like performance status lack numeric definitions.
